samples.summary: New ghost-cleanup loop in `moveRangeTo` iterates attacker-controllable `spillRows` × `spillCols` with an awaited store read per iteration — unbounded work from shared-document data (client DoS)
samples.evidence:
The delta adds, inside the merge-propagation pass, a nested loop bounded only by the destination cell's own `spillRows`/`spillCols` fields (sheet.ts:2402-2412), performing `await this.store.get(ghostRef)` for every (dr,dc) — for every covered cell of every moved merge, all inside the open batch started at sheet.ts:2320.

Those fields are not derived locally: they are read straight back out of the collaborative Yorkie document. `YorkieStore.normalizeCell` copies `spillRows`/`spillCols` through with no range, integrality or magnitude check (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:231-236), and nothing on the read path validates them either.

Vector: any collaborator with write access to the document (or a tampered/imported workbook) sets a single cell to `{v:'x', spillRows: 1e9, spillCols: 1e9}` somewhere in the sheet. When another user drags a merged block whose destination covers that cell, the loop at 2402 attempts up to 1e18 awaited store reads, wedging the victim's tab indefinitely (the batch opened at 2320 stays open until `endBatch` in `finally`, which is never reached). The victim's own selection size does not bound the work — the attacker's cell field does. The same unbounded pattern exists at sheet.ts:1053 and 1128 (`setData`/`removeData`), so this is a new instance of an existing class rather than a new class, but it is a new reachable site added by this delta. I could not confirm exploitability beyond collaborator write access (an attacker who already has write access can also destroy data directly), hence low confidence; a clamp such as `Math.min(cell.spillRows, MAX_SPILL)` would remove the amplification.

samples.summary: No bounds/shape validation on `MergeSpan` or spill dimensions read from the shared document, while this delta widens how much work they drive
samples.evidence:
`YorkieStore.getMerges` shallow-copies every `{rs, cs}` from the collaborative doc with no validation (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:997-1005), and `safeWorksheetRecordEntries` only guards against duplicate-key errors (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-record.ts:47-61). `mergeCoveredSrefs` (sheet.ts:856-862) loops `r < anchor.r + span.rs`, so a span of `Infinity`/huge value from a peer is an unbounded generator.

This delta adds two new enumerations driven by that data: line 2370 enumerates every covered sref of each moved AND overwritten merge, and line 2391 adds every covered sref of the relocated merge to `changedSrefs` unconditionally (previously only cells that actually existed and were cleared were added). The resulting set is fed to `expandChangedSrefsWithMergeAliases` → `buildDependantsMap` → `calculate` (2431-2433), so the recalculation set now scales with merge AREA rather than with touched cells.

I could not turn this into a full DoS at the new lines: the containment checks at sheet.ts:2294 and 2301 reject the move unless each merge fits inside the (user-selected) source/destination range, which bounds the enumeration by the victim's own selection. The unvalidated span remains reachable unbounded through `rebuildMergeCoverMap` (sheet.ts:770) / `loadMerges` (sheet.ts:496), which this delta does not touch. Reporting the missing validation because the delta increases reliance on these values; a validating `getMerges` (finite, positive, integer, clamped to sheet dimensions) would close both.

samples.summary: Ghost deletion during a move reaches cells arbitrarily far outside both the source and destination ranges, with the reach chosen by unvalidated cell data
samples.evidence: `ghostRef = { r: ref.r + dr, c: ref.c + dc }` (sheet.ts:2405) walks up to `spillRows` × `spillCols` away from a destination cell, i.e. well outside the range the user dragged. The only integrity check is `ghostCell?.spillAnchor === sref` (2407) — a claim stored in the shared document, not something the local session established. A collaborator who stamps `spillAnchor: '<anchor sref>'` onto unrelated cells and sets a large `spillRows`/`spillCols` on the anchor makes an innocuous drag-move silently delete those distant cells (2408), outside the operation's visible scope and outside undo expectations. Impact is bounded because the attacker already needs document write access, so this is hardening rather than privilege escalation; scoping the ghost sweep to the sheet's used bounds, or to a validated spill rectangle, would contain it.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as quoted (sheet.ts:2400-2412 loops over cell.spillRows × cell.spillCols with an awaited store.get per iteration inside the batch opened at 2320), and yorkie-store.ts:231-236 does pass the fields through unvalidated. However the finding is not blocking under the Security lens rubric. (1) Its impact is availability/resource exhaustion (unbounded iteration), which is outside the enumerated lane: no authorization gate is bypassed, no secret exposed, no injection sink reached (the tainted value only becomes a loop bound), no crypto check weakened, no SSRF/deserialization/path traversal. (2) The sole precondition is write access to the shared collaborative document, i.e. a peer at the same trust level as the victim who can already destroy the document's data directly — no privilege boundary is crossed. (3) The claimed "tampered/imported workbook" vector does not exist: an exhaustive grep shows the only writers of spillRows/spillCols are the calculator itself from evaluated spill dimensions (calculator.ts:122-123, 136) and a pass-through copy in style-mutation.ts:70-75; no import/deserialization path sets them. (4) The identical unbounded loop already sits on the primary recalculation path (calculator.ts:74-85 and the ghost-write loop at 137-143), which any peer edit triggers, so the new site adds no new trust boundary or attacker capability — clamping spill dimensions is a robustness/hardening item for the correctness lens, at most minor here, not a security merge blocker.
